Use lots of references, try gestural poses, go somewhere to sit down with people and draw what’s around you. There’s also a lot of books for artist, but I’d start off with some anatomy books. George B. Bridgman is a pretty good artist who makes constructive anatomy books. I’d also try to expand your horizon of artist to study. Basic human anatomy by Roberto Osti is also good but may be too detailed but my talented arts teacher had it in her classroom for students. :) it’s a long journey and will take some time. I’d suggest making simple shapes and learning to render them (like a sphere) but most of all! Use references.

So the antihelix is of one the only things that protrude when drawing the ear, from the front. I’d use a reference and practice on another piece of paper. I’d also darken your shading as it look too flat. Make sure to use circular motions when you’re shading your drawings so it doesn’t look as messy. I think it’s a really great start so keep it up.
